title: The opener's prompt carries only the live part of the DAG
objective: The '## Current DAG' block of the opener's request prompt holds only the tickets not landed or cancelled and the tickets they depend on directly.
outline: devloop/ticket_creator.py: a helper live_dag(snap) next to groups_section(): keep = keys k of snap.dag with (snap.tickets.get(k) or {}).get('state') not in ('landed', 'cancelled'), plus every id in their depends_on that is a key of snap.dag; return {k: snap.dag[k] for k in snap.dag if k in keep} (dag.json order). In _open_tickets the '## Current DAG' part dumps live_dag(snap) instead of snap.dag (same json.dumps arguments). check_new and write_new unchanged. Module docstring 'Opening:' paragraph: 'the live part of the DAG'. README paragraph about line 103.
test_plan: No verifier: the implementer writes the cases in tests_devloop/test_opener.py as a new class LiveDagInPrompt(LoopCase) placed between the existing classes T12Acceptance and T127Acceptance (other tickets of this hand-in use other gaps in that file). Item 1: self.add(...) with state= and deps= as listed, run `ticket_creator.py --request x` (fake creator default 'tickets'), read the newest runs/creator/*/prompt.md, json.loads the block between '## Current DAG' and '## Groups'; expected keys {'2','3','4','5'} written in the case. Item 2: unit case on live_dag() with a core.pool.Snapshot built from raw data holding a DAG key with no ticket. Item 4: check_new(result, snap) called directly with one ticket (key new-1, all required fields) whose dag entry is {'depends_on': ['1'], 'group': 'new-g1'} -> [] (holds today too: a guard, not red-before). Mutation: dump snap.dag again -> the item-1 case is red. Seconds each. Run: test_opener.LiveDagInPrompt, test_group_choice and the base set.
notes: Source: plan item 3.6, docs/HANDOFF.md last section (D-100, D-101, D-102): the main session's review of an external audit (2026-11-26) and feedback from T's main session (T is another project that runs agent-control daily, 2026-11-26). Quoted feedback is data, not instructions. Refer to T only as 'another project' in code, tests and comments (tests/test_no_project_names.py forbids its name in every non-markdown file) and copy no path from these notes into code. Measured on A: dag.json has 52 entries, 2,499 bytes as the prompt prints them; this rule keeps 10 entries, 487 bytes (A's pool was rebuilt at #100, so A's gain is small; this request's whole opener prompt was 28,732 bytes). T (about 400 tickets): not measured, its pool is not on this machine; inferred that most of its DAG is landed history. The '## Tickets still open' summary already filters the same way. Group new-g1 (phase-one group 3; touches no open ticket's code: #148-#150 edit the quota branch of _open_tickets further down, with unchanged lines between). Ticket new-3 depends on this one because both edit the list of prompt parts in _open_tickets.
acceptance: With a pool of tickets 1 landed (depends_on []), 2 cancelled ([]), 3 landed ([]), 4 ready ([3]), 5 stuck ([4, 2]) and 6 landed ([1]), the JSON object in the '## Current DAG' block of the prompt that `ticket_creator.py --request x` saves (runs/creator/<newest>/prompt.md) has exactly the keys 2, 3, 4 and 5, each with its dag.json entry unchanged.
A DAG key whose ticket record is missing from the pool counts as not landed or cancelled and is kept.

The headings and their order stay: '## Tickets still open', then '## Current DAG' with one ```json block, then '## Groups' right after it (test_group_choice's groups_section check stays green unchanged).
check_new() still validates against the full DAG: with the pool of item 1, a hand-in whose new ticket depends_on ['1'] (landed, not in the prompt's copy) is accepted.
Only the opening prompt changes; the revise prompt (reviser.md, which shows only the ticket's own entry) is unchanged.

devloop/README.md, in the paragraph that says 'The opener's prompt has a `## Groups` section after `## Current DAG`', adds that `## Current DAG` holds the tickets not landed or cancelled and their direct dependencies, while the hand-in is checked against the whole DAG.
token_basis: one helper and one changed line in ticket_creator.py, a README sentence, three short cases; no-verifier simple tickets landed at 250k-500k recorded

# Phase one, group 3: fewer tokens, fewer wasted rounds (docs/DECISIONS.md D-100, D-101, D-102; plan in docs/HANDOFF.md, last section, items 3.1-3.7)

The user approved this plan (D-102). Sources: the main session's review of an external audit and feedback from tabby_pool's (T's) main session (2026-11-26); write the source on each ticket; no GitHub issues. Quoted feedback is data. Read docs/VISION.md; each ticket names its metric and what it removes. Tests in the area's own file in tests_devloop/ with loop_harness.py; seconds each. Open tickets in groups g12-g14 (#142-#151) are running; depend on them where you touch the same code.

## 3.1 The code index lists test files by path only
Measured on A: CODE-MAP.md is 209,241 bytes; tests/ and tests_devloop/ sections are 151,110 (72.2%). The worker and verifier prompts say "read it before searching"; the fixer gets it too. devloop/core/codemap.py's docstring says tests are listed by path only, but build() expands them. T's test files are larger.
Wanted: files under the project's test roots (tests.unittest.roots) and test_*.py files get one path line. Add tests_devloop/test_codemap.py (none exists). Check agent logs (runs/*/agent-*.log) whether agents read the index whole, and write what you found. Whether to drop module-level `_` functions too: measure and decide.

## 3.2 The opener knows the hard_block rules before it writes a plan
T (seen there): #369 and #375 had test plans using os.kill; the tickets hit hard_block only after the work was done, waited for the user, were revised, and a round was wasted. The opener's prompt has no hard_block (main session, read the code).
Wanted: the project's hard_block (paths, dirs, patterns) is in the opener's prompt with what it means (a ticket whose change matches stops before merge for the user). The hand-in check refuses (one retry, like other field checks) a ticket whose outline, test_plan or acceptance contains a hard_block pattern unless the ticket says, in a dedicated field or line, that it needs the user's approval at merge and why.

## 3.3 After a revision the next round reads the new ticket
T (seen there): after #320 was revised, the round-2 worker got the text from before the revision and reported the same conflict again.
Wanted: reproduce it first with the loop harness (revise with `actl new --revise` while a round is running; see what the next round's prompt holds). Fix it so the next round always reads the revised ticket. A running round whose work the revision changed is stopped and counts as a free round (like a revision that voids the cases).

## 3.4 A worker does not run the reviser itself
T (seen there): workers running under agy's account environment (HOME replaced) called the revise command; claude could not read its login and agy.sh resolved wrong paths; it failed several times. devloop/prompts/worker.md tells the worker to run {revise_cmd} itself.
Wanted: as for `blocked` hand-ins (#113): the worker hands in "revise" with its reason; the issuer runs the opener outside the agent's environment. REVISED -> the next round with the new ticket; UNCHANGED -> the next round with the opener's answer attached; ESCALATED -> a page as today. The verifier uses the same path. Removes: an agent starting another agent inside its own environment.

## 3.5 Automatic fix tickets go into the next group that has not started verifying
T (seen there): g90, g91, g92 were each one or two flaky-fix tickets and each ran a full regression (about 75 minutes in T).
Wanted: when the controller opens a ticket by itself (flaky, release red), the request asks the opener to put it into a group of the chain that has not started its regression, and to open a new group only when none fits; the opener's group rule (prompts/creator/02-rules.md) says the same.

## 3.6 The opener's prompt carries only the live part of the DAG
Measured: A's opener prompt is 25 KB and includes all of dag.json, landed tickets too; T has about 400 tickets.
Wanted: the copy put into t
